title: Skill behavioural evals (evals.json)
$comment: Behavioural-eval spec consumed by run_skill_evals.ts (scaffold/aggregate/report) and counted by skill_eval_coverage.ts. Distinct from triggers.json (activation/routing axis). Roadmap: road-to-skill-eval-coverage Phase 1. Assertion kinds mirror _grade_assertions() in run_skill_evals.ts exactly — add a kind there before adding it here.

skill.description: Skill slug; must match the parent skill directory name (evals/ lives under src/skills/<skill>/).

_calibration.description: Optional free-text note recording calibration status / provenance (e.g. uncalibrated finding_floor placeholders). Advisory; ignored by the grader.

skill_body_sha.description: Optional SHA-256 of the skill's SKILL.md body at the time these evals were authored/last verified. When present, lint_behavioural_eval_freshness flags the eval stale if the current SKILL.md sha differs — the body changed, so the eval may no longer exercise it. Absent = unpinned (out of scope for the staleness gate), mirroring lint_eval_freshness's upstream:null handling.

scenarios.description: One or more behavioural cases. Each pairs a prompt fixture with deterministic pass/fail assertions on the produced output.

id.description: Stable scenario slug, unique within this file (run directories are named by it).

prompt.description: The input fixture handed to the skill under test.

_why.description: Optional rationale: why this fixture exists at all. Annotation, never input — nothing reads it at run time, and it carries the same underscore prefix as the top-level `_calibration` to say so. Added because the alternative, on scenarios whose rationale IS the negative-control argument for the pair above them, was to delete the argument to satisfy additionalProperties.

environment.description: Optional precondition note (v2, additive) — the environment the scenario assumes (e.g. 'a git repo with an open PR', 'quality.local_auto_run: true'). Advisory context for the runner/operator; not graded.

requires_human.description: Optional (v2, additive). When true, the scenario cannot be auto-graded in CI — the runner skips it and reports `manual-pending` (NEVER a silent pass). Pair with human_instructions.

human_instructions.description: Optional (v2, additive). Steps for a human to grade a requires_human scenario.

assertions.description: Pass/fail checks on the output. Prefer deterministic kinds (contains/file_exists/finding_floor); use rubric only where a deterministic check is impossible, and pin the judge as a known limit.

path.description: Path (run-relative or absolute) the skill must have produced (deterministic).

n.description: Minimum number of findings the output must carry (counted deterministically). 0 is a trivially-passing floor (the grader passes when count >= n) — used where the case only guards against over-reporting.

pattern.description: Optional regex counted globally; without it, markdown list-item lines are counted (see _count_findings).

criterion.description: Natural-language pass criterion graded by a sub-agent. NON-deterministic — the grader returns pass:null until a pinned judge fills it. Use only where no deterministic check exists; record the judge as a known limit.

must_use.description: Tool names the run MUST have called (checked against <run_dir>/tool-trace.json). v2, additive.

must_not_use.description: Tool names the run MUST NOT have called. v2, additive.

oneOf.$comment: Evaluated against the recorded tool trace. No trace present → pass:null manual-pending, never a silent pass.

n.description: Ceiling on meaningful steps = tool calls net of retries (a call repeating the immediately-preceding call name is a retry, not a step). Counted from <run_dir>/tool-trace.json; no trace → manual-pending. v2, additive.
